source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

hinge.title: Decide whether repeated parts form mathematical symmetry by identifying a fold or rotation transformation that maps the figure onto itself.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Definite pattern is the label that belongs on this item, so 'Decide whether repeated parts form mathematical symmetry by' is answered as definite pattern rather than symmetry.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: symmetry still holds here even though a specific fold or rotation relation must be identified is missing from the stem — on the item about Decide whether repeated parts form mathematical.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Definite pattern is what produces symmetry, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards — on the item about Decide whether repeated parts form mathematical.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: The symmetry rule also covers this: Do not require group-theory language, so it is not an exception — on the item about Decide whether repeated parts form mathematical.

intelligence.enrichment: A figure is symmetric when repeated parts occur in a definite pattern that matches under a fold or rotation, not merely because the figure is attractive or has repeated motifs.
